inspection_summary: Inspected all 2,151 splitlines from title through references. The source develops a continuous-to-discrete spectral mechanism for a finite-rank interaction added to the quantized xp Hamiltonian: phase-space boundary deformations encode counting fluctuations, boundary states implement transport, a Jost-like determinant separates scattering from embedded bound states, Fourier/Mellin duality reproduces completed-L-function phases, and Riemann-Siegel data supplies a candidate fluctuation function. The paper explicitly leaves decisive analyticity, nonvanishing, classical-limit, and off-critical-zero questions unresolved. Displayed formulas are mostly recoverable with their prose but retain PDF-layout risk and require original-PDF verification before formula-faithful downstream use.

sections_inspected.label: Title, abstract, and publication front matter
sections_inspected.mathematical_role: States the proposed semiclassical boundary deformation, exact quantum solution, duality mechanism, and claimed conditional spectral realization.

sections_inspected.label: I. Introduction
sections_inspected.mathematical_role: Motivates the Hilbert-Polya, trace-formula, random-matrix, quantum-chaos, Berry-Keating, and Connes perspectives and locates the paper's intended reconciliation.

sections_inspected.label: II. Semiclassical approach
sections_inspected.mathematical_role: Derives smooth xp counting, compares prime-orbit fluctuations, generalizes phase-space boundaries, and formulates the inverse reconstruction and its monotonicity obstruction.

sections_inspected.label: III. From classical to quantum
sections_inspected.mathematical_role: Defines the Hermitian antisymmetric finite-rank interaction and interprets it as boundary-to-boundary transport producing closed and open trajectories.

sections_inspected.label: IV. Exact solution of the Schroedinger equation
sections_inspected.mathematical_role: Solves the generic model, constructs the determinant F, distinguishes scattering and embedded bound states, and illustrates confinement and resonance by a trap.

sections_inspected.label: V. Analyticity properties of F(E)
sections_inspected.mathematical_role: Uses Fourier and Cauchy representations to infer upper-half-plane analyticity and a lower-half-plane restriction on nonreal zeros.

sections_inspected.label: VI. Quantum version of the Berry-Keating model
sections_inspected.mathematical_role: Maps hard classical boundaries to Fourier-dual wavefunctions, derives completed-L-function phases, and obtains asymptotic smooth-zero resonances.

sections_inspected.label: VII. Generic quantum fluctuation construction
sections_inspected.mathematical_role: Promotes semiclassical fluctuation constraints to operator equations, solves both boundary states, and conditionally reduces the Jost function to a counting phase.

sections_inspected.label: Riemann-Siegel connection and prime comparison
sections_inspected.mathematical_role: Factors the critical-line zeta expression through dual boundary data, extracts a candidate fluctuation phase, and compares its truncated sum heuristically with prime products.

sections_inspected.label: Berry-Keating smoothing, approximate functional relation, and limitations
sections_inspected.mathematical_role: Replaces the discontinuous Riemann-Siegel truncation by a smooth exact representation, notes a noncritical-line extension, and states the assumptions that prevent an RH proof.

sections_inspected.label: Acknowledgments
sections_inspected.mathematical_role: Nonmathematical attribution and funding material inspected for completeness.

sections_inspected.label: VIII. Appendix A: wave functions and norms
sections_inspected.mathematical_role: Reexpresses eigenfunctions in the free basis, derives bound-state norms and orthogonality, and gives smooth and numerical exact-zero wavefunctions.

sections_inspected.label: References and terminal page matter
sections_inspected.mathematical_role: Bibliographic support only; no new source argument.

accepted_units.title: Two spectral pictures from quantum chaos and Connes's sign objection
accepted_units.why_material: Connects self-adjoint spectral realization, Selberg-style classical/quantum duality, GUE time-reversal breaking, prime-labelled periodic orbits, and Connes's minus-sign objection to the alternative picture of zeros as missing continuum levels; this frames the paper's embedded-state reconciliation target.
accepted_units.context_note: The span is conceptual setup rather than evidence that the desired operator exists.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Low: the reusable content is stated in prose; displayed fluctuation formulas occur later.

accepted_units.title: Planck-cell regularization reproduces the smooth Riemann zero count
accepted_units.why_material: Shows how bounding the unbounded xp flow by position and momentum cutoffs makes the subenergy phase-space area finite and yields the leading smooth zero-count asymptotics.
accepted_units.context_note: The agreement is semiclassical and asymptotic, not an exact spectral identification.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Medium: the area rule and asymptotic formulas are central; verify equations (2.3)-(2.5) against the retained PDF before formula-faithful reuse.

accepted_units.title: Prime-orbit analogy and its two mismatches
accepted_units.why_material: Separates the smooth count from the zeta-dependent fluctuation, compares its formal prime expansion to a periodic-orbit trace expression, and records the period, instability, time-reversal, sign, and finite-winding mismatches that any quantum-chaos model must confront.
accepted_units.context_note: The prime sum on the critical line is explicitly heuristic because the Euler product does not converge there.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: High: several displayed sums carry the comparison, although the prose recovers their roles; original-PDF verification is required.

accepted_units.title: Deforming the xp phase-space boundaries while preserving exchange symmetry
accepted_units.why_material: Introduces positive curved position and momentum boundaries as carriers of spectral fluctuations and formulates the scaled exchange symmetry that links them.
accepted_units.context_note: This is a semiclassical ansatz with a unique intersection assumed, not derived.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Medium: the boundary inequalities and symmetry equation should be checked against the retained PDF.

accepted_units.title: Boundary geometry determines the fluctuation density
accepted_units.why_material: Computes the allowed area for general boundaries, isolates the correction to Berry-Keating counting, and shows that under exchange symmetry the logarithmic boundary displacement is fixed by the derivative of the fluctuation count.
accepted_units.context_note: The conclusion depends on the semiclassical area prescription and imposed exchange symmetry.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: High: integration limits and equations (2.18)-(2.26) are layout-sensitive; verify them in the original PDF.

accepted_units.title: Monotonic inverse reconstruction versus multivalued boundaries
accepted_units.why_material: Turns a prescribed fluctuation density into a boundary function when the energy-position map remains monotone and identifies strong curvature of the fluctuation count as the condition producing multivalued, discontinuous boundary branches.
accepted_units.context_note: Uniqueness is only semiclassical and conditional on the stated monotonicity inequality.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Medium: the mechanism is clear in prose, but equations (2.27)-(2.29) require PDF verification.

accepted_units.title: Finite-rank antisymmetric interaction as the quantum boundary model
accepted_units.why_material: Quantizes xp on the positive half-line and adds an interaction built from two real boundary states; Hermiticity and antisymmetry yield a real paired spectrum and connect the two wavefunctions to the classical boundary roles.
accepted_units.context_note: The correspondence between boundary curves and wavefunctions is proposed heuristically at this stage.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Medium: operator ordering and signs in equations (3.1)-(3.6) must be verified against the PDF.

accepted_units.title: Boundary transport closes allowed trajectories and opens forbidden ones
accepted_units.why_material: Interprets the rank-two interaction as projection-and-transfer between boundary states, with an inverse supplied by Hermiticity; classically the transfer closes allowed xp trajectories while the inverse channel yields unbounded forbidden-region trajectories, anticipating embedded bound states in a continuum.
accepted_units.context_note: The classical-to-quantum transport identification is a physical heuristic, not a derivation of a classical interaction Hamiltonian.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Medium: prose preserves the mechanism; coordinate maps and energy-preservation equations should be PDF-checked.

accepted_units.title: Reconciling Berry-Keating levels with Connes missing lines
accepted_units.why_material: Contrasts lower-cutoff discrete counting with Connes's upper-cutoff continuum and proposes embedded discrete states as a single quantum structure capable of realizing both spectral interpretations.
accepted_units.context_note: The span states the target reconciliation, whose realization depends on the later exact solution.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Low: the conceptual contrast is prose-grounded; the displayed Connes count should be checked if quoted.

accepted_units.title: Logarithmic-coordinate solution and the shuffle identity
accepted_units.why_material: Transforms the Schroedinger problem into a first-order equation in log position, expresses the solution through boundary overlaps and endpoint amplitudes, and derives paired ordered-integral representations whose change of integration order gives a shuffle relation.
accepted_units.context_note: The asymptotic endpoint interpretation assumes decay conditions on the transformed boundary functions.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: High: nested integrals, Fourier conventions, and matrix entries are extraction-sensitive and require original-PDF verification.

accepted_units.title: Jost determinant separates scattering states from embedded bound states
accepted_units.why_material: Defines the determinant F from the overlap system, derives its reality symmetry, and shows that nonzero F leaves nonnormalizable endpoint amplitudes while real zeros cancel both endpoints and can produce normalizable bound states embedded in a full real scattering continuum.
accepted_units.context_note: Normalizability at a zero of F still requires suitable boundary-state decay, as the source notes.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: High: determinant signs and coefficient formulas must be verified against the retained PDF; the prose securely supports the zero-versus-scattering distinction.

accepted_units.title: Quantum trap: fine tuning converts resonances into confined embedded states
accepted_units.why_material: Uses delta-localized boundary states to show concretely that a coupling-product condition creates periodic or antiperiodic embedded levels, confines their wavefunctions to a finite interval, and turns them into resonances when the tuning is relaxed.
accepted_units.context_note: The example illustrates the general transport mechanism and only matches semiclassical levels asymptotically.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: High: delta normalizations, coupling signs, and energy formulas need original-PDF verification.

accepted_units.title: Cauchy representation imposes Jost analyticity and zero location
accepted_units.why_material: Rewrites the ordered overlap as a Cauchy transform, linking causal ordering to analyticity in the upper energy half-plane and restricting zeros of F to the real axis or lower half-plane.
accepted_units.context_note: The source assumes sufficiently well-behaved Fourier transforms and refers out for the detailed zero-location proof.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: High: distributional signs and half-plane conventions are formula-sensitive and must be checked in the PDF.

accepted_units.title: Fourier-dual hard boundaries generate completed-L-function phases
accepted_units.why_material: Associates the position cutoff with a delta boundary state and the momentum cutoff with cosine or sine states, then uses Mellin transforms to show that their exchange duality contributes the gamma-factor phases of even and odd Dirichlet L-functions.
accepted_units.context_note: Reality of the boundary state forces the parity split; the construction reproduces phase data rather than the full L-functions.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: High: Fourier normalizations, parity phases, gamma ratios, and Mellin conventions require retained-PDF verification.

accepted_units.title: Pole subtraction converts the gamma phase into the Berry-Keating Jost function
accepted_units.why_material: Splits the completed-zeta phase into upper-half-plane analytic and pole parts, evaluates the required Hilbert transforms, and obtains a Jost function whose leading high-energy form is one plus a phase factor.
accepted_units.context_note: The final simple form is asymptotic and retains corrections of order inverse energy.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: High: residue coefficients, analytic-half-plane assignments, and signs in equations (6.14)-(6.22) require PDF verification.

accepted_units.title: Coupling choice turns smooth zero counts into resonances
accepted_units.why_material: Shows that a tuned coupling product makes real-axis zeros of the asymptotic Jost function track either the average Riemann count or a shifted cosine-phase count, and interprets these smooth locations as asymptotic bound states or, more accurately, resonances.
accepted_units.context_note: This is only a smooth, high-energy approximation and not a realization of exact zeros.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: High: phase and sign choices in equations (6.23)-(6.26) must be checked against the PDF.

accepted_units.title: Quantized fluctuation constraint solves the position-boundary state
accepted_units.why_material: Promotes the semiclassical logarithmic boundary relation to an operator equation, diagonalizes the free xp generator, and solves the resulting first-order energy equation so that the Mellin transform of one boundary state acquires the prescribed fluctuation phase.
accepted_units.context_note: The operator equation is an ansatz defining the boundary state and assumes an odd fluctuation function.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: High: operator ordering, delta-derivative signs, and transform conventions require original-PDF verification.

accepted_units.title: Half-line momentum extensions solve the dual boundary state
accepted_units.why_material: Defines log absolute momentum through self-adjoint extensions of squared momentum on the half-line, uses cosine and sine bases to solve the second boundary equation, and recovers the Fourier duality between both boundary wavefunctions for arbitrary fluctuations.
accepted_units.context_note: Only the Neumann and Dirichlet extension choices are pursued despite the larger extension family.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: High: overlap phases and the differential solution are formula-layout sensitive and require retained-PDF verification.

accepted_units.title: An analyticity assumption collapses the Jost function to a counting phase
accepted_units.why_material: Combines the fluctuating boundary transforms, assumes the total counting phase is analytic and decaying in the upper half-plane, and conditionally reduces F to a simple phase expression whose zero count matches the semiclassical fluctuation formula.
accepted_units.context_note: The analyticity and decay premise is assumed rather than established and is later identified as a central gap.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: High: the exponential phase, Cauchy integral, coupling normalization, and additive counting constant require PDF verification.

accepted_units.title: Dual boundary data factor the critical-line zeta function
accepted_units.why_material: Uses the exchange transformation of the two boundary amplitudes and the zeta functional relation to propose a duality-invariant sum, yielding a factorization of the Riemann-Siegel Z function into an amplitude and cosine of the candidate counting phase.
accepted_units.context_note: The proportionality factor may itself have zeros or poles, so zero coincidence is not automatic; simplicity is also only expected.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: High: phase conventions and the factorization equations require original-PDF verification.

accepted_units.title: Riemann-Siegel truncation supplies a candidate fluctuation phase
accepted_units.why_material: Matches cosine and sine components of the Riemann-Siegel main sum to define a finite Dirichlet sum f, extracts its argument as the fluctuation function, and distinguishes its smooth interpolation and truncation-induced jumps from the exact step count.
accepted_units.context_note: The construction initially drops the Riemann-Siegel remainder, so its numerical agreement is an approximation rather than independent validation.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: High: truncation bounds, branch choices for the logarithm, and phase signs must be verified against the PDF.

accepted_units.title: Truncated Dirichlet sum versus truncated Euler product
accepted_units.why_material: Explicitly notes that the critical-line Euler product is invalid, then compares the finite Riemann-Siegel sum with a finite prime product and reports only qualitative alignment of extrema and phases, isolating a possible but unproved prime-information channel.
accepted_units.context_note: This is a naive numerical heuristic; unequal term sets and lack of convergence prevent an Euler-product identification.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Medium: prose carries the caution and conclusion; product and cutoff definitions should be PDF-checked.

accepted_units.title: Berry-Keating smoothing gives an exact dual decomposition
accepted_units.why_material: Replaces the discontinuous main-sum cutoff by contour-defined smooth weights, obtains a smooth exact f and the dual decomposition of zeta, and identifies the error-function leading approximation for improved numerical evaluation.
accepted_units.context_note: The contour, branch cut, and smoothing parameter are essential; higher terms remain necessary for controlled accuracy.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: High: contour placement, kernel exponent, and summation formulas are extraction-sensitive and require the retained PDF.

accepted_units.title: Approximate functional relation as phase-space splitting beyond the critical line
accepted_units.why_material: Interprets the two sums in the Hardy-Littlewood approximate functional relation as position and momentum lattice contributions along the xp energy hyperbola and suggests that moving off the critical line corresponds to an imaginary non-Hermitian shift of the xp Hamiltonian.
accepted_units.context_note: The off-critical Hamiltonian link is a suggestion, not a demonstrated spectral equivalence.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: High: exponents, error terms, and left/right eigenfunction powers require original-PDF verification.

accepted_units.title: Why the construction does not prove RH
accepted_units.why_material: Identifies the unproved upper-half-plane analyticity and decay of the counting phase, the needed nonvanishing of f on the real axis, the merely partial zeta-as-Jost factorization, and the missing classical interpretation of the interaction and primes.
accepted_units.context_note: The paper expressly claims support rather than proof and cannot exclude off-critical zeros.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Medium: the caveats are prose-grounded; equation (7.64) should be PDF-checked before formal use.

accepted_units.title: Bound-state wavefunctions, orthogonality, and density-of-states norm
accepted_units.why_material: Reexpresses eigenfunctions in the free-energy basis, separates distributionally normalized scattering states from localized zero-of-F states, and uses Jost analyticity to derive orthogonality and a norm proportional to the derivative of the counting function.
accepted_units.context_note: The simplified norm formulas require the stated phase-factor and analyticity assumptions.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: High: principal-value integrals, coefficient signs, dispersion relation variables, and normalization constants require original-PDF verification.

accepted_units.title: Residue construction for smooth-zero wavefunctions
accepted_units.why_material: Specializes the boundary phases to the smooth Riemann count, evaluates the bound-state integral by residues, and relates decay at infinity to the smooth phase-zero condition while contrasting forbidden-region and oscillatory components.
accepted_units.context_note: These energies are smooth approximations and the plotted profiles do not establish exact spectral realization.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: High: the hypergeometric expression is visibly layout-sensitive and must be verified against the retained PDF; prose supports only its qualitative behavior.

accepted_units.title: Truncated integral for exact-zero candidate wavefunctions
accepted_units.why_material: Explains that no analytic exact-zero wavefunction is obtained and instead truncates the boundary-state integral numerically, reporting both shared structure with the smooth states and additional irregular behavior.
accepted_units.context_note: The numerical profiles depend on an explicit finite integration cutoff and are illustrative rather than a convergence or normalizability proof.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: High: the truncated integral and cutoff convention require original-PDF verification.

within_source_synthesis_candidates.title: Boundary geometry to finite-rank quantum transport
within_source_synthesis_candidates.claim: The paper's central bridge maps deformed classical exclusion boundaries first to a fluctuation density and then to two boundary states whose antisymmetric rank-two coupling realizes energy-preserving transport between those boundaries.
within_source_synthesis_candidates.limit: The curve-to-wavefunction correspondence and the classical meaning of the interaction are heuristic, and the later exact model does not derive that bridge from an underlying classical Hamiltonian.

within_source_synthesis_candidates.title: Embedded-state Jost architecture
within_source_synthesis_candidates.claim: Endpoint cancellation at zeros of an analytic Jost-like determinant converts a continuum xp problem into possible normalizable embedded states, while the determinant phase controls scattering and its derivative controls bound-state norm.
within_source_synthesis_candidates.limit: Existence and normalizability depend on boundary decay and analyticity assumptions; the source does not show that every desired Riemann zero satisfies them.

within_source_synthesis_candidates.title: Exchange duality becomes the completed-zeta functional phase
within_source_synthesis_candidates.claim: Cosine/sine Fourier duality between position and momentum boundary states becomes a Mellin-space gamma-factor phase and supports a duality-invariant critical-line factorization patterned on the zeta functional equation.
within_source_synthesis_candidates.limit: This recovers phase symmetry and a proposed factorization, not the zeta function as an independently established spectral determinant.

within_source_synthesis_candidates.title: From smooth counting to a fluctuation-bearing Jost phase
within_source_synthesis_candidates.claim: A single conceptual pipeline takes smooth semiclassical xp counting, encodes departures through boundary displacement, lifts the displacement to phases of boundary transforms, and uses a Riemann-Siegel-derived phase to place candidate Jost zeros near the exact count.
within_source_synthesis_candidates.limit: The final reduction of the Jost function requires an unproved analytic-decay condition, and the initial Riemann-Siegel construction is truncation-dependent.

within_source_synthesis_candidates.title: Riemann-Siegel smoothing and the nonvanishing bottleneck
within_source_synthesis_candidates.claim: Smoothing the Riemann-Siegel truncation gives an exact dual decomposition in terms of f, but the desired zeta-as-Jost conclusion additionally requires f to remain nonzero and the induced total phase to have the correct upper-half-plane behavior.
within_source_synthesis_candidates.limit: Those properties are not proved, so the construction supplies a conditional spectral model rather than an RH argument.

within_source_synthesis_candidates.title: Prime information is sought through two incompatible representations
within_source_synthesis_candidates.claim: The source first expresses prime information through a divergent critical-line periodic-orbit analogy and later through qualitative agreement between a finite Dirichlet sum and finite Euler product, leaving the primes' classical role in the quantum interaction unresolved.
within_source_synthesis_candidates.limit: Neither comparison establishes a convergent prime expansion or a classical Hamiltonian whose periodic orbits are the primes.

within_source_synthesis_candidates.title: Fine tuning distinguishes embedded states from resonances
within_source_synthesis_candidates.claim: Both the finite trap and the Berry-Keating specialization show that cancellation of scattering amplitudes requires a tuned coupling-phase relation; relaxing exact cancellation naturally changes putative bound states into resonances.
within_source_synthesis_candidates.limit: The trap is illustrative and the Berry-Keating result is asymptotic, so it does not prove exact Riemann zeros are stable bound states.

Further segmentation would predominantly split algebraic derivations already enclosed by coherent units, repeat summaries and figure captions, or select reference/front matter; formula-faithful reuse remains gated on retained-PDF verification.
stop_reason: Reached the end of the source after accounting for the complete semiclassical-to-quantum construction, the generic and Riemann-specific Jost mechanisms, the appendix normalization logic, and the paper's explicit unresolved analyticity, nonvanishing, classical-limit, and off-critical-zero limitations; only acknowledgments, references, repeated summaries, figure-only material, and routine formula manipulation remain outside accepted units.
